title: Number of Ways to Select Buildings
statement:
A street is described by the binary string `s`: building `i` is an office when `s[i]` is `'0'` and a restaurant when `s[i]` is `'1'`. You want to choose three buildings at positions `i < j < k` such that, reading them from left to right, no two neighbours in the chosen trio have the same type (so the trio spells `"010"` or `"101"`).

Return how many such trios of positions exist. Two choices differ when their sets of positions differ.
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every trio of positions is O(n³). Instead, look at the middle building of a valid trio: if it is a `'0'`, the outer two must both be `'1'`, one on each side, and any left `'1'` pairs with any right `'1'`. So a middle `'0'` contributes (ones to its left) × (ones to its right), and a middle `'1'` contributes (zeros to its left) × (zeros to its right). Running prefix counts give all of these in one pass.

## Approach

1. Count `totalZeros` in the whole string; `totalOnes` is the rest.
2. Walk left to right keeping `zerosLeft` and `onesLeft`, the counts strictly before `i`.
3. At a `'0'`, the ones after it are `onesRight = totalOnes - onesLeft`; add `onesLeft * onesRight` to `ways`, then count this zero in `zerosLeft`.
4. At a `'1'`, do the mirror: add `zerosLeft * zerosRight`, then bump `onesLeft`.
5. Return `ways`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "001101"` has `totalZeros = 3`, `totalOnes = 3`.

| i | s[i] | left count | right count | added | ways |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 0 ones | 3 ones | 0 | 0 |
| 1 | 0 | 0 ones | 3 ones | 0 | 0 |
| 2 | 1 | 2 zeros | 1 zero | 2 | 2 |
| 3 | 1 | 2 zeros | 1 zero | 2 | 4 |
| 4 | 0 | 2 ones | 1 one | 2 | 6 |
| 5 | 1 | 3 zeros | 0 zeros | 0 | 6 |

The answer is `6`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass to count zeros and one pass over the middles.
- Space: O(1): only a handful of counters.

## Pitfalls

- Update `zerosLeft` or `onesLeft` after using it, so the middle building is not counted as its own neighbour.
- The answer can reach about n³/27, far beyond 32 bits for n = 10^5; Java and C need a 64-bit total and 64-bit products.
- The chosen buildings need not be neighbours on the street: `"0110"` has two valid trios, (0, 1, 3) and (0, 2, 3), although no three adjacent characters alternate.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `totalZeros`, `totalOnes` | how many offices and restaurants the whole street has |
| `zerosLeft`, `onesLeft` | how many of each type appear before index `i` |
| `onesRight`, `zerosRight` | how many of the opposite type appear after index `i` |
| `ways` | number of valid trios counted so far |

narration.3: Start counting offices so the number after any point can be derived later.
narration.4: First pass: look at every building once.
narration.7: Whatever is not an office is a restaurant.
narration.11: Second pass: treat each building as the middle of a trio.
narration.12: A middle office needs a restaurant on both sides.
narration.13: Restaurants to the right are all restaurants minus those already seen.
narration.14: Every left restaurant pairs with every right restaurant, so add the product.
narration.15: Now this office joins the offices on the left.
narration.17: A middle restaurant needs an office on both sides; count the offices to its right.
narration.18: Add the number of left-office, right-office pairs around it.
narration.19: This restaurant joins the restaurants on the left.
narration.22: Every possible middle was handled, so the total is the answer.
